summary: QA pass for 'GO N1-N2 follow-up fixes' (Fix #1-4 + Manual Checks 5-6). Re-verified Fix #1/#2 by code review (no changes needed, already correct). Wrote new backend test file test_notetaker_followup_fixes.py (14 tests) covering Fix #3 full-lock and Fix #4 legacy-consent-incomplete; all pass. Full regression suite (test_notetaker_phase1.py + test_notetaker_tasks.py + new file) = 87/87 passed. Exercised every UI flow requested with real browser automation against the live preview and captured all requested screenshots: legacy APPROVED consultation (pill + notice + disabled revise + enabled export/copy), CONSENT_WITHDRAWN lock screen (no Cancel/Consent buttons, no network call to /note), the version-conflict UI screen (Check 5), and the full approve -> revise -> edit -> re-approve -> withdraw UI walkthrough with differing content hashes (Check 6). No regressions found. One minor spec-letter deviation found and documented (not fixed, as it's an edge-case judgment call for the main agent) in POST /note/approve's pre-existing idempotency shortcut.

minor.issue: When a legacy-consent-incomplete consultation is already APPROVED and the caller passes the SAME expected_version as the current approved_version, the pre-existing idempotency shortcut (lines ~1472-1481 of advocate_notetaker_router.py) returns 200 {already_approved:true} BEFORE the _guard_legacy_consent() 409 check is ever reached. This is a literal (minor) deviation from the spec line 'POST /note/approve ... now return 409 ... when this flag is true' -- in practice it causes NO data mutation (it just echoes the existing approved_version/content_hash back), so there is no real security/integrity impact, but it is not technically a 409 as the spec states for every approve call on a legacy-flagged record. Calling approve with a DIFFERENT (non-matching) expected_version on the same legacy record does correctly hit a 409 (via the pre-existing 'already_approved_different_version' branch, not the legacy-guard branch, but still a 409 with a blocking message). Verified via test_approve_same_version_is_idempotent_not_blocked / test_approve_different_version_blocked_409_legacy_message in test_notetaker_followup_fixes.py.

spec_item_results.Fix1_reverify: PASS (code review only, no UI regression needed per main agent's context note; also visually re-confirmed incidentally during Check 6: the withdrawn participant 'TEST Check6 Client' showed a single row with a 'Withdrawn' badge in the Manage Consent modal, no duplicate rows).
spec_item_results.Fix2_reverify: PASS (code review) - grepped advocate_notetaker_router.py for '[advocate edit]'; the stripping logic is confined to GET-path read-time helpers and no PATCH/generate/revise write path re-inserts the marker; content_hash computation is untouched by any read-time shim (also re-confirmed by the pre-existing TestLegacyNoteShim pytest passing).
spec_item_results.Fix3_backend_full_lock: PASS - fresh consultation taken to NOTE_DRAFT, withdrawn: GET consultation returned locked:true, locked_reason set, manual_notes/note_draft/approved_version all null, note_versions=[]; GET /note -> 403; GET /export -> 403; GET /consent -> 200 with full history (2 records incl. withdrawal); POST /manual-notes and POST /note/generate both still 409 via pre-existing state-machine checks (not a new code path, as spec required).
spec_item_results.Fix3_frontend_lock_screen: PASS - screenshot confirmed CONSENT_WITHDRAWN screen shows lock icon (🛡), explanatory text, no Cancel button, no 'Consent' manage-button in header, and zero /note network requests fired after load.
spec_item_results.Fix4_backend_legacy_label_and_block: PASS - used the pre-existing TEST_Consult_Manual / d8d0cbe2-3388-4186-90c1-72f7318a76be (state APPROVED, legacy_consent_incomplete:true) exactly as referenced in the spec. GET consultation returns legacy_consent_incomplete:true. POST /note/revise -> 409 'Consent incomplete (legacy): ...'. POST /note/approve with a non-matching expected_version -> 409 (different message, see minor finding above). GET /export still returns 200 (policy: viewing/exporting already-approved content stays allowed).
spec_item_results.Fix4_frontend_notice_and_pill: PASS - screenshot of the same legacy consultation shows the yellow 'Consent incomplete (legacy)' notice box on ApprovedStep (with the exact guidance text about recording a fresh 'given' decision or withdrawing), the 'Consent incomplete (legacy)' pill next to the 'Approved' StatusPill in the header, the 'Revise this note' button replaced entirely by the notice (effectively disabled), and Export/Copy buttons both rendered ENABLED (not greyed) exactly per the 'only block new edits, not viewing/exporting' policy.
spec_item_results.ManualCheck5_version_conflict_UI: PASS - created a fresh NOTE_DRAFT consultation, loaded v1 in the browser UI, used a parallel direct API call to save a conflicting v2 (simulating a second session/tab) before the UI's own save, then edited and tapped 'Save edits' in the UI. The UI correctly caught the 409 and rendered the in-app conflict screen verbatim: 'This note changed' / 'Reapply my edits' / 'Discard my edits and load version 2' -- never silently overwrote.
spec_item_results.ManualCheck6_approve_revise_withdraw_UI: PASS - full UI walkthrough: generated v1, approved it (screenshot: 'Approved' pill, hash 26794a0b07a7e3d7), tapped 'Revise this note', edited an item, saved, approved the new version (screenshot: hash changed to 437b4cf72b2f7bca, confirmed different from v1's hash -- proves approved_version snapshot is per-version not a live pointer), then revised once more and withdrew consent via the in-app 'Manage consent' modal. Final screenshot shows the CONSENT_WITHDRAWN lock screen with zero Approve/Save/Cancel/Consent actions visible anywhere on the page.

action_items: Optional/minor: consider whether POST /note/approve's idempotency shortcut should also check _legacy_consent_incomplete before returning its 200 echo, for strict literal compliance with the spec wording ('POST /note/approve ... returns 409 ... when this flag is true') -- functionally harmless today since it only echoes unchanged data, so this is a judgment call, not a blocker.
No other blocking issues. Ready for founder sign-off on N1-N2 follow-up fixes as far as this QA pass's checked items go.
critical_code_review_comments: advocate_notetaker_router.py remains at ~1767 lines (grew further this batch) -- still recommend splitting into matters/consent/notes/export/tasks sub-routers in a future refactor pass, not blocking.
_apply_lock() and _legacy_consent_incomplete()/_guard_legacy_consent() are well-commented with explicit founder-decision context inline -- good practice, made this review faster.
